messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticed a QoS regression on the reranker embeddings endpoint after yesterday's kernel selector change. QPS steady at ~90 instead of 150 at peak, and token p99 spiked.
emily: :eyes: which selector did we flip? auto_select -> fused_attn_v2??
sam: We moved default from 'fused_attn_v1' to 'auto' so runtime picks v2 on A100s. Change was in commit 5c3b.
rahul: Any change in input shape / vector dims? reranker uses 768d vectors; did batch packing change?
sam: No vector dim change. Batching heuristic did kick in — avg batch size increased from 2.1 -> 3.7 which *should* help, but latency went up.
jane: Posting the last 5min token latency breakdown from observability:
jane: ```
route: /v1/rerank/embeddings
qps: 92 -> 88
token_latency_p50: 45ms -> 62ms
token_latency_p95: 180ms -> 315ms
token_latency_p99: 210ms -> 420ms
```
matt: From infra side, no NVLINK/PCIe saturation alerts. GPU util up slightly.
ops-bot: perf-profile attached: /artifacts/1764002345/profile-zip
emily: Can we get a flamegraph? I suspect KV cache build or attention kernel fallback path. Recent kernel selector picks 'attn_generic' for some seq lengths.
rahul: We saw similar with seq_len=1024 -> some kernels degrade. Most rerank requests are short (seq ~ 128). Any change in prompt padding or tokenization?
sam: We did start batching multi-candidate inputs differently — concatenated with separators increased effective seq length by ~40 tokens.
emily: Ok that explains kernel mismatch. If the selector sees avg_seq=168 it might choose different kernels with worse memory access patterns.
jane: I pulled a profile on a degraded instance — hot stacks:
jane: ```
1) attention_kernel::build_kv_cache 42.1ms
2) attention_kernel::compute_attention 110.4ms
3) kv_cache::serialize 24.0ms
4) cudnn_sgemm fallback 53.9ms
```
rahul: compute_attention 110ms is big for short seq. Looks like we're hitting non-fused code path.
emily: Quick mitigation: pin kernel selection to fused_attn_v1 for the rerank model route only. Can we rollout a canary config?
matt: Yep, canary policy ready. I can push a route override to test on 10% traffic.
sam: Please do. Also add tracing to record selected kernel name and seq_len per request (token-level metadata).
jane: I'll add a per-route KPI panel: kernel_name, avg_seq_len, batch_size, qps, p99 token latency.
rahul: Also check KV cache hit rate — if our concatenation prevents cache reuse across candidates we lose prefix cache gains.
emily: Good point. Add metric: kv_prefix_hit_rate and avg_prefix_cache_size.
ops-bot: Canary deploy started on 10% -> monitoring.
matt: Canary shows qps back to ~140 on the canary nodes, p99 down to ~230ms. Baseline still low.
sam: That's promising. If canary holds for 5m, roll to 50%.
emily: I'll open a follow-up issue to revise batching heuristic: cap effective seq_len influence and prefer kernel stability for short routes.
rahul: Also note: embedding vector dim 768 unchanged. Batch size in canary is ~2.3 — closer to pre-change.
jane: Saved dashboard snapshot: /dash/embeddings/rerank/kernel-breakdown/1764002345
sam: Thanks all. Next actions: roll canary -> monitor 10min -> if stable, roll 100%. Emily to update batching heuristic PR, Jane to add panels, Rahul to validate KV caching logic.
emily: ACK
rahul: ACK
jane: ACK
matt: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Canary rolled to 50% at 1764002402
